subject: MSA / Order Form: SLA — downtime exclusions, weekend maintenance carveouts & P1 credit cap
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena@octagon.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Brian Cho <brian.cho@octagon.com>
Date: 2029-08-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SLA asks for MSA/order form (uptime targets, maintenance carveouts)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the call yesterday. I've attached a short summary of the uptime/credits language Octagon needs to move the order form to procurement (attachment: Octagon_SLA_Request.pdf). High level: we need clarity on the weekly maintenance policy and an assurance that any weekly maintenance scheduled outside a previously agreed blackout window will not be counted against uptime.

Key asks:
- Uptime target: 99.95% platform-wide (month) — acceptable?
- Maintenance carveouts: allow two rolling maintenance windows per month (up to 3 hours each) with 72h calendar notice; anything beyond should be treated as unplanned outage.
- P1 response: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes; remediation SLO aligned to impact tiering — propose financial credit scale (see attached).
- Cap on service credits: total monthly credit cannot exceed 25% of that month’s invoice (we may need to cap per incident).

Can you confirm Redwood's willingness to reflect these in the MSA/order form or point me to your legal contact for redlines? Procurement needs the language in a tracked doc by EOW next week.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Director of IT Ops
Octagon Health
Attachment: Octagon_SLA_Request.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Garcia <elena@octagon.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-08-07T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks for MSA/order form (uptime targets, maintenance carveouts)

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the doc. I looped in Marissa (account lead) and Lauren (legal) to get the redline moving. A few quick notes from the commercial side before legal digs in:

- 99.95% monthly is within our standard commitment for this tier; we'll confirm the exact credit banding.
- We typically allow maintenance carveouts but prefer scheduling maintenance in a defined blackout calendar (customer-specified blackout hours) to avoid ambiguity. Two rolling windows per month, 3 hours each sounds workable with the 72h notice request — we'll propose language that preserves a fallback for emergency maintenance.
- P1 ack within 15 minutes is doable for on-call; remediation timelines will be tier-dependent. We usually model credits by % of monthly invoice per incident with a monthly cap — Marissa and I flagged the 25% cap request for legal/finance review.

Lauren — can you take the attached Octagon doc and produce a tracked redline we can iterate on? If helpful, Marissa and I can propose a pragmatic credit matrix (we have a template).

Next step: Lauren to share redline; I'll schedule a quick alignment call with Octagon for Wednesday.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Elena Garcia <elena@octagon.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-08-08T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks for MSA/order form (uptime targets, maintenance carveouts) — redline attached

Hi Elena (and team),

Thanks for sharing the asks. Attached is a tracked redline to the MSA + order form (file: Redline_MSA_OrderForm_LB.docx). I summarized the discrete legal points below so procurement has a short checklist:

1) Uptime Measurement and Exclusions — we can accept 99.95% monthly if the calculation excludes scheduled maintenance windows and excludes customer-caused downtime (per section). Proposed edit: define "Scheduled Maintenance" with minimum 72 hours' notice and a maximum of two windows/month of up to 3 hours each; add an emergency maintenance carveout with notification "as soon as practicable" and right to use safeguard measures.

2) Service Credits — we will use a per-incident credit table tied to monthly uptime buckets. We are open to a monthly aggregate cap; however, a 25% cap of monthly invoice is unusually high for platform tiers at scale. Proposed compromise: cap monthly credits at 15% but allow the parties to negotiate a higher cap tied to committed spend tiers. We also propose a per-incident cap so a single incident cannot consume the monthly cap.

3) Response & On-call — we can confirm an initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes for P1 incidents where customer has an active emergency channel (PagerDuty or similar). Remediation SLAs are operational and will include definitions for P0/P1/P2 with time-to-resolution windows in the order form.

4) Blackout Windows / Customer-specified hours — recommend we capture customer blackout hours in the order form appendix so maintenance scheduling is explicit.

5) Audit & Evidence — customer may request post-incident logs for confirmed incidents; propose a 30-day window for evidence requests and a separate scope/fee for extended retention.

Elena — if those guardrails look reasonable I can post the redline in the shared doc and accept comments. I also attached a quick credit matrix (sla-credit-matrix.xlsx) with the proposed bands and caps.

-Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redline_MSA_OrderForm_LB.docx (docx, 95KB)
Attachment: sla-credit-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)

From: Elena Garcia <elena@octagon.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Brian Cho <brian.cho@octagon.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-08-10T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks for MSA/order form (uptime targets, maintenance carveouts)

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear edits and the compromise language. Internal procurement reviewed the 15% cap suggestion; they're willing to accept 15% if we can add an exception: if Octagon provides a committed annual spend threshold (to be included in the order form), the parties can re-open the cap for a higher negotiated amount. That gives us the flexibility we need for the pilot year.

One specific ask from operations: weekend blackout windows. For patient-impacting maintenance we need a hard blackout between Fri 18:00 PT and Sun 23:59 PT for a subset of services (see doc appendix). Can Redwood reflect a per-service appendix identifying which services fall under that blackout?

Also please confirm that emergency maintenance that impacts uptime will be accompanied by a root-cause and remediation plan within 72h.

If we can get a tracked doc updated, I'll coordinate procurement sign-off and route to our legal for a final pass.

Regards —
Elena

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Garcia <elena@octagon.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-08-13T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks for MSA/order form (uptime targets, maintenance carveouts) — mutual action plan

Elena / team — quick alignment & next steps from our side: 

1) Lauren has posted the tracked redline to the shared doc (link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cSLA-redline). Please review the changes; we highlighted the cap/credit language and the Appendix section for per-service blackout entries.
2) We're comfortable with the amended monthly credit cap of 15% as a default with the contract-level exception you requested (we'll add a clause to reopen if committed annual spend threshold is met).
3) Weekend blackout: we can include a per-service appendix; ops will need Octagon to identify the service list so we can lock the appendix into the order form before signature.
4) Emergency maintenance: we will commit to an RCA + remediation plan within 72 hours for incidents that materially affect uptime.

Action items: 
- Octagon: confirm service list for weekend blackout and respond to the shared doc comments by 2029-08-16.
- Redwood (Marissa/Karthik): provide final credit matrix and example per-incident cap by 2029-08-15.
- Legal: prepare signature-ready MSA+Order Form once Octagon confirms appendix entries.

I'll open a 30-minute sync Wed 8/14 11:00 PT; if that works we can close remaining items and move to DocuSign. If not, let me know alternate windows.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
